ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The graph of the linear function $y = ax + b$ (where $a$ and $b$ are constants, with $a \neq 0$) is shown as in the diagram. What is the solution to the equation $ax + b = 0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Method 1: It can be seen from the graph that the coordinates of the intersection points of the line with the coordinate axes are $(0, -1)$ and $(2, 0)$,\\
substituting $(0, -1)$ and $(2, 0)$ into the linear function $y=ax+b$ yields: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}0=2a+b\\ -1=b\end{array}\right.$,\\
solving this gives $\left\{\begin{array}{l}a=\frac{1}{2}\\ b=-1\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \frac{1}{2}x-1=0$, solving for $x$ gives $x=2$,\\
$\therefore$ the solution of the equation $ax+b=0$ is $x=\boxed{2}$;\\
Method 2: According to the fact that the abscissa of the intersection point of the linear function $y=ax+b$ with the x-axis is the solution of the linear equation $ax+b=0$, it is known that the solution is $x=\boxed{2}$.
